children: Ujjivan Small Finance Bank shares extended their decline on Wednesday, falling up to 10 percent in two trading sessions.
The stock was quoted at Rs 62.41 per share on the NSE, down 4.51 percent, at around 1:20 pm.

Ujjivan Small Finance Bank shares, which had risen 2 percent on Monday, began declining in the previous session after the company said its board had approved the request for early retirement of MD and CEO Sanjeev Nautiyal on health grounds.
Nautiyal, a former deputy managing director of SBI, was appointed MD and CEO of Ujjivan Small Finance Bank (SFB) for three years with effect from July 1, 2024.
In an email dated August 31, 2026, Nautiyal expressed his desire to seek early retirement from the bank with a three-month notice period, the lender said in a regulatory filing.
The board considered Nautiyal's request for early retirement and, in view of his health issues, respected his decision and approved his request, the filing said.

He will be on leave from September 1, 2026, until the expiry of his notice period on November 30, 2026. Nautiyal will cease to be the MD and CEO and Key Managerial Personnel of the bank with effect from September 1, 2026, it said.

Based on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, the board approved the appointment of Executive Director Carol Furtado as acting MD and CEO with effect from September 1, 2026, subject to approval from the Reserve Bank of India, it said.
Carol is a key member of the leadership team that laid the foundation and built Ujjivan throughout its journey.
The board will initiate the process of identifying a successor to Sanjeev Nautiyal and submit its recommendation to the RBI in due course.
